'''David M. Arnold''' (August 9, 1939 – January 3, 2021) was an American mathematician, formerly the Ralph and Jean Storm Professor of Mathematics at [[Baylor University]],<ref name="Baylor">{{cite web |title=Math Department Mourns Loss of David Arnold |url=https://www.baylor.edu/math/news.php?action=story&story=223015 |website=Baylor University |date=14 April 2021 |access-date=4 June 2021 |archive-date=July 29, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729123556/https://www.baylor.edu/math/news.php?action=story&story=223015 |url-status=live }}</ref> and also a published author of 10 books, currently held in 1,886 libraries.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n78011753/ |title=Arnold, David M. |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=August 6, 2016 |archive-date=August 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816103534/https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n78011753/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Education and career==
He received his master's degree from [[Western Washington University]] and his Ph.D. at [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], the latter had [[Joseph J. Rotman]] as his advisor. Other professorships he has held are Professor of Mathematics at [[New Mexico State University]] and visiting professor at [[University of Washington]], [[University of Connecticut]], [[University of Essen]] and [[Florida Atlantic University]].<ref name="Baylor"/>

== Personal life ==
He was "well-loved" by his wife Betty, his 5 children, his 13 grandchildren, and his 6 great-grandchildren.<ref name="Baylor" /> He enjoyed his family, reading, and [[birding]].<ref name="Baylor" />
